title: The Snail and the Rose Tree
summary: In the center of the garden stood a blooming rose tree, bursting with fragrant red blossoms. At its root lived a snail, safely curled within his slimy shell....
keywords: the snail and the rose tree
full_text:
In the center of the garden stood a blooming rose tree, bursting with fragrant red blossoms. At its root lived a snail, safely curled within his slimy shell.

"What do you give to the world?" hissed the cynical snail. "You merely bloom and drop your petals! You have no deep philosophy! I spit upon the world; I withdraw into myself, for I am self-contained!"

The rose tree smiled gently in the morning sunshine: "I bloom because my heart is full of gratitude! The sun warms me, the dew refreshes me, and my perfume brings joy to little children and solace to the sick. I give all that I have received. What do you give from your shell?"

"I give nothing," said the snail coldly, "for the world is unworthy of me." And he shut himself up tight.

The rose tree blossomed year after year, blessing all who passed; while the selfish snail dried up in his shell, forgotten and useless in the dust.
moral: To give oneself in love and beauty is the highest joy; selfish isolation rots in its own shell.
